destination_record.name: Uttarakhand
destination_record.tagline: Ganga aarti in Haridwar and Rishikesh, white-water rafting, cool hill stations at Mussoorie and Nainital, and tiger country at Jim Corbett.
destination_record.places: Haridwar, Rishikesh, Mussoorie, Dehradun, Nainital, Bhimtal, Jim Corbett National Park; Auli and Kedarnath on request

on.places: Rishikesh and Haridwar for aarti and rafting, Mussoorie, Nainital and Bhimtal for cool hill weather, and Jim Corbett from mid-November. The Char Dham shrines, including Kedarnath, open around late April or May and close around Diwali.
on.activities: River rafting (best from March to June and from mid-September to November), Ganga aarti, sightseeing and short walks in the hill stations, boating on Naini Lake and cable car rides. October and November bring clear air and fine mountain views. Summers are hot in the plains and pleasant in the hills.

off.places: Haridwar, Rishikesh and the hill stations can still be visited, but this is the monsoon. Hill roads see landslides, most of the Corbett safari zones are closed and the higher shrines are hard to reach.
off.activities: Temple visits, spa stays and quiet resort time. River rafting is suspended during the monsoon, roughly July to mid-September, and Jim Corbett's main safari zones are closed from about mid-June to mid-November. Hill roads can be blocked for hours or days, so plan buffer time. The Kanwar Yatra in July and August makes Haridwar and Rishikesh very crowded.

mid.places: Haridwar, Rishikesh, Jim Corbett and Dehradun are comfortable by day and cold at night. Mussoorie and Nainital are cold and can see snow, and Auli is the main snow destination.
mid.activities: Wildlife safaris at Corbett, Ganga aarti, temple visits and cosy hill stays. Mussoorie and Nainital are quiet and cold, with occasional snowfall and fog, and Auli's ski season usually runs from January to March. Rafting is possible but the water is cold. The Char Dham shrines are closed for winter.

profile.overview:
Uttarakhand sits on the Himalayan foothills and the upper Ganga, and few states pack in so much within a few hours of Delhi. You can watch the evening Ganga aarti at Haridwar and Rishikesh, raft through rapids on the river, walk the Mall Road at Mussoorie, row on Naini Lake in Nainital and look for tigers in Jim Corbett National Park, all in one holiday.

It is easy to reach from Delhi and works well for families, friends, couples and senior parents. Roads in the hills are winding and the monsoon brings landslides, so the season matters. Tell us your dates, group size and budget, and we will build the itinerary around you.

facts.capital: Dehradun (winter capital); Gairsain is the summer capital
facts.languages: Hindi, Garhwali and Kumaoni; English in tourist areas
facts.climate: Plains and foothills about 5°C to 40°C; hill stations about 0°C to 30°C; heavy rain from July to September
facts.flight_time: Delhi to Dehradun (Jolly Grant) about 1 hr by air; from Chennai usually one stop, 5 to 6 hr in all. Haridwar and Dehradun are major railheads.

reasons.title: Ganga, faith and adventure
reasons.text: Evening aarti at the ghats and rapids on the same river, often within a single day in Rishikesh.

reasons.title: Hill stations close to the plains
reasons.text: Mussoorie and Nainital offer cool air, lakes, ropeways and mountain views a few hours from Dehradun and Kathgodam.

reasons.title: Wildlife at Jim Corbett
reasons.text: India's oldest national park offers jeep safaris through sal forest and grassland, with tigers, elephants and many birds.

reasons.title: Easy from the major cities
reasons.text: Jolly Grant airport, Dehradun and Haridwar railheads and Kathgodam station keep transfers short.

reasons.title: Year-round choices
reasons.text: Rafting and hill stations suit summer, Corbett suits winter, and the Char Dham yatra runs from late April or May to October or November.

attractions.title: Har Ki Pauri, Haridwar
attractions.text: The best-known ghat on the Ganga, where the evening aarti draws thousands of pilgrims and visitors.

attractions.title: Ram Jhula and Laxman Jhula, Rishikesh
attractions.text: Riverside areas on both banks of the Ganga with cafes, ashrams and shops. The old Laxman Jhula bridge has been closed for safety, so we confirm the current position.

attractions.title: Mall Road and Gun Hill, Mussoorie
attractions.text: Mussoorie's famous promenade and a ropeway-served viewpoint with mountain views on clear days.

attractions.title: Kempty Falls, Mussoorie
attractions.text: A popular waterfall on the road from Mussoorie, with pools below that families enjoy in the warmer months.

attractions.title: Naini Lake, Nainital
attractions.text: A crescent-shaped lake ringed by hills, with boating, the Mall Road and the Naina Devi temple on its shore.

attractions.title: Bhimtal and Sattal
attractions.text: Quieter lakes a short drive from Nainital, good for a relaxed boat ride and a picnic.

attractions.title: Jim Corbett National Park
attractions.text: Founded in 1936, it is India's oldest national park and a favourite for tiger and elephant sightings by jeep.

attractions.title: Auli and Kedarnath (on request)
attractions.text: Auli is a ski and mountain-view resort and Kedarnath a high Himalayan shrine at about 3,583 m. Neither is in our standard packages, and both depend on season, road and weather.

experiences.title: Ganga aarti at dusk
experiences.text: Lamps, chants and floating diyas at Har Ki Pauri in Haridwar or Triveni Ghat in Rishikesh.

experiences.title: White-water rafting in Rishikesh
experiences.text: A guided run through rapids on the Ganga, with safety gear and a trained boatman, in the open season only.

experiences.title: Jeep safari in Jim Corbett
experiences.text: A morning or afternoon drive through the park's safari zones, subject to permit availability and season.

experiences.title: Boating on Naini Lake
experiences.text: A slow row or paddle boat ride at Nainital, best in the morning or at sunset.

experiences.title: Cable car and viewpoints
experiences.text: Ropeway rides at Mussoorie and Nainital for mountain views, depending on weather and operating days.

experiences.title: Yoga and riverside camping
experiences.text: Morning yoga and a night at a riverside camp near Rishikesh, with a campfire where permitted.

food.title: Garhwali thali
food.text: Local dishes such as kafuli, a spinach curry, chainsoo, a black lentil dish, and jhangora kheer, a sweet made from millet.

food.title: Kumaoni aloo ke gutke
food.text: Spiced boiled potatoes with local herbs, often served with bhatt ki churkani, a soybean curry.

food.title: Bal mithai and singori
food.text: Kumaoni sweets, a fudge coated in sugar balls and a milk sweet wrapped in a leaf, sold in Nainital.

food.title: Momos and chai on the Mall
food.text: Hot momos, maggi and tea are classic Mussoorie and Nainital snacks on a cool evening.

food.title: Vegetarian and Jain meals
food.text: Haridwar and the temple areas of Rishikesh are vegetarian and largely alcohol-free, and we can arrange Jain meals on request.

tips.title: Plan around the monsoon
tips.text: From July to September landslides can block hill roads for hours or days. Keep buffer time and avoid tight flight or train connections after hill drives.

tips.title: Know the Char Dham season
tips.text: Kedarnath, Badrinath, Gangotri and Yamunotri open around late April or May and close around Diwali. Registration is required and rules change, so we confirm at booking.

tips.title: Reach the ghats early for aarti
tips.text: Har Ki Pauri and Triveni Ghat fill up well before dusk. Arrive 45 minutes early for a good spot, and keep bags light.

tips.title: Respect the holy towns
tips.text: Haridwar and the temple areas of Rishikesh are vegetarian and alcohol-free. Dress modestly at ghats and temples.

tips.title: Book Corbett safaris in advance
tips.text: Safari permits are limited and issued against a valid photo ID. Most zones close from about mid-June to mid-November.

tips.title: Pack for cold nights
tips.text: Hill stations can be cold at night even in summer, and from November to February they are very cold. Carry layers and motion-sickness tablets for winding roads.

travel_info.visa: Indian citizens need no visa for Uttarakhand. Carry a valid government photo ID such as an Aadhaar card, passport, voter ID or driving licence, which hotels and permits need. Entry to Jim Corbett's safari zones needs a permit booked against ID in advance, and the Char Dham yatra needs registration. We arrange permits and confirm the current rules at booking.
travel_info.health: No compulsory vaccinations. Hill roads are winding, so carry motion-sickness tablets. Mussoorie and Nainital are around 2,000 m, which most people find comfortable, but shrines such as Kedarnath (about 3,583 m) and Auli can cause altitude sickness. Drink bottled or filtered water, and note that rafting has age and health limits.
travel_info.money: ATMs are available in Haridwar, Rishikesh, Dehradun, Mussoorie and Nainital but are scarce in remote areas. UPI works in most towns, though mobile networks can be patchy in the hills, so carry some cash for small shops, ghat offerings and tips.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit Uttarakhand?
faqs.a: March to June and October to November suit most trips. December to February is cold with snow in the higher hills and is good for Corbett. July to September is the monsoon, with landslide risk on hill roads.

faqs.q: How many days do I need?
faqs.a: Four to five nights covers Haridwar, Rishikesh and Mussoorie, or Nainital and Jim Corbett. Six to seven nights lets you combine them at an easier pace.

faqs.q: Can I visit Kedarnath with Indian Rounds?
faqs.a: Kedarnath is not part of our standard packages. The shrine opens around late April or May and closes around Diwali, needs registration and involves a trek of about 16 km from Gaurikund or a helicopter. We can plan it on request, subject to season and road conditions.

No. Rafting at Rishikesh is suspended during the monsoon, roughly from July to mid-September, and the water is cold in winter. The season is best from March to June and from late September to November.

faqs.q: How do I reach Uttarakhand from Chennai?
faqs.a: Fly to Dehradun's Jolly Grant airport, usually with one stop, or to Delhi and continue by train or road. Haridwar and Dehradun are the main railheads, and Kathgodam is the railhead for Nainital.

group_trips.title: Ganga Aarti, Rafting and Mussoorie Group Trip
group_trips.summary: Seven days from Haridwar's Ganga aarti to Rishikesh rafting and the hill views of Mussoorie, with a trip captain and an easy pace.
group_trips.overview:
This group trip follows the Ganga from the plains into the foothills over six nights: one in Haridwar, two in Rishikesh, two in Mussoorie and a last night in Dehradun. You see the evening aarti at Har Ki Pauri, spend a day on the water at Rishikesh and then climb to Mussoorie for Kempty Falls, Gun Hill and the Mall Road.

A trip captain travels with the group, and vegetarian and Jain meal options are available on request. Breakfast and dinner are included at the hotels, and the pace is relaxed, which suits families, friends travelling together and senior parents.

Departures run in the dry season only. Rafting depends on river levels and is not available during the monsoon, and hill roads can be affected by weather.

group_trips.summary: A long weekend with Ganga aarti and white-water rafting in Rishikesh, then a night in the hills at Mussoorie, travelling in a small group.
group_trips.overview:
This short break fits the river and the hills into four easy days. You arrive in Rishikesh for the Ganga aarti, spend a day rafting and relaxing by the river, and then drive up to Mussoorie for Kempty Falls and an evening on the Mall Road before a late departure.

The pace is deliberately gentle, with one headline activity a day. A trip captain travels with the group, and vegetarian and Jain meal options are available on request.

Rafting runs in the open season only and depends on river levels, and hill roads can be slow after heavy rain.

honeymoon_trips.title: Corbett and Nainital Honeymoon: Jungle Safari, Lakeside Evenings and Candlelight
honeymoon_trips.summary: Five unhurried nights for two, with a jeep safari near Jim Corbett, boat rides on Naini Lake, a couples spa session and a candlelight dinner in Nainital.
honeymoon_trips.overview:
This private honeymoon pairs the forests of Jim Corbett with the lakes of Nainital: two nights near the national park and three in Nainital. You travel by private car throughout, start most mornings late and keep the evenings for each other.

At Corbett, the signature outing is a jeep safari through sal forest and grassland, subject to permit availability and season. In Nainital you take a boat ride on Naini Lake, ride the cable car to Snow View Point and make a day trip to the quieter Bhimtal lake.

Expect a flower welcome and bed decoration on arrival, a couples spa session and a candlelight dinner, all subject to availability. Please share your wedding date at booking so the hotels can arrange the welcome. This trip runs from November to June, when the safari zones are open.

custom_trips.title: Classic Uttarakhand: Haridwar, Rishikesh and Mussoorie
custom_trips.summary: A private five-night circuit with Haridwar's Ganga aarti, Rishikesh rafting and the hill views of Mussoorie.
custom_trips.overview:
This classic private circuit takes you from the Ganga ghats to the hill station of Mussoorie in five nights. You see the evening aarti at Har Ki Pauri, explore Rishikesh and spend a day on the river, then travel up to Mussoorie for Kempty Falls, Gun Hill and the Mall Road.

It works for families, couples and friends who want a first look at Uttarakhand without a rushed schedule. Departure dates and the pace are flexible, and the price shown is a sample starting price.

This trip is best from March to June and from October to November. Rafting is not available in the monsoon.

Mansa Devi temple, with an optional ropeway ride
Ram Jhula and Laxman Jhula areas and Triveni Ghat aarti in Rishikesh

custom_trips.title: Nainital, Bhimtal and Jim Corbett Family Holiday
custom_trips.summary: A private four-night family trip with boating at Nainital and Bhimtal, a cable car ride and a jeep safari near Jim Corbett.
custom_trips.overview:
This family trip pairs two nights in Nainital with two near Jim Corbett National Park. In Nainital you take a boat ride on the lake, ride the cable car to Snow View Point and visit the quieter lake at Bhimtal, then drive towards Corbett via Kaladhungi, where Jim Corbett's old home is now a museum.

The next morning is a jeep safari through the park, with time to rest and enjoy the resort grounds afterwards. The pace is easy, with short drives and plenty of breaks, which suits children and grandparents.

This trip is offered from November to June, when the Corbett safari zones are open.
highlights: Boat ride on Naini Lake and a stroll on Mall Road
Cable car ride to Snow View Point, subject to operation
Bhimtal Lake and a relaxed day by the water
Jim Corbett Museum at Kaladhungi on the drive
Jeep safari at Jim Corbett National Park, subject to permit and season

custom_trips.title: Rishikesh Adventure: Rafting, Riverside Camp and Yoga
custom_trips.summary: A private three-night break in Rishikesh with white-water rafting, a riverside camp stay, morning yoga and the Ganga aarti.
custom_trips.overview:
This active private break keeps you in and around Rishikesh for three nights. You raft through rapids on the Ganga, sleep at a riverside camp, start a morning with yoga and finish with the evening aarti at Triveni Ghat.

It suits friends, young travellers and anyone who wants a few days of fresh air on a modest budget. Optional adventure activities such as a giant swing or cliff jumping can be added on request, subject to operator availability and age and health limits.

Rafting runs in the open season only, from about mid-September to June. Ask for a quote for your dates and group size.

Riverside camp stay with a campfire where permitted
